Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home , Lucknow Counsel for Applicant :- Satish Kumar Sharma Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
Heard Sri Harendra Singh holding brief of Sri Satish Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State.

It has been contended by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in jail since 9.6.2024 in Case Crime No. 305 of 2024 u/s 457, 376, 323, 504 & 506 IPC, P.S. Taal Gaon, District Sitapur.
It has been submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged.
Attention has been drawn towards impugned F.I.R. which has been lodged on 27.8.2024 for the incident dated 20.4.2024 pursuant to the application being filed u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C.

Even for the alleged incident dated 20.4.2024 the application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C.

1 has been lodged on 13.6.2024 and no proper explanation of the aforesaid delay has been given.

sentences.text: In the F.I.R. The allegation has been made against three persons but except the present applicant final report has been submitted against two other accused persons.
He has further submitted that after recording her statement u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. she was asked to undergo medical examination, she refused to get her medically examined.
Learned counsel has stated that since the entire story was false and misconceived and the victim is a married lady of 25 years, therefore, she deliberately refused medical examination.

Further, in the cases where the allegation of rape has been levelled the medical examination is mandatory requirement, failing which the offence of rape may not be established beyond all reasonable doubt.
He has further submitted that one more allegation was levelled against the present applicant has made clip of obscene video of victim but no such evidence was found.
The applicant has no prior criminal history and the charge-sheet has been filed in this case.

The learned counsel for the applicant has given an undertaking on behalf of applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings and shall abide by all terms and conditions of bail, if granted.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant.

Without entering into the merits of the case and considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, contents and allegations of the F.I.R., the fact that F.I.R. has been lodged on 27.8.2024 for the incident dated 20.4.2024 pursuant to the application being filed u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. but no proper explanation of the aforesaid delay has been given, after recording her statement u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. the prosecutrix was asked to undergo medical examination but she refused to get her medically examined, allegation was levelled against the present applicant that he has made clip of obscene video of victim but no such evidence was found, the applicant has no prior criminal history and the charge-sheet has been filed in this case and the undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.
Bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant Ateek, involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Ateek vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home , ... on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23593409/
2 trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text:
(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The applicant shall not leave the country without permission of the Court concerned.
.
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 11.11.2024
